references.text: The lamb chosen on the tenth day is to be kept until the fourteenth day, when it shall be slaughtered.
Moses repeats the instruction to take a lamb for each family for the Passover celebration.
The congregation of Israel is mentioned as recipients of God's instructions through Moses.
Requirements for sacrificial animals from the small livestock, either lambs or goats, that must be without defect.
The Israelites celebrated Passover in Gilgal and took lambs as prescribed by the law.
King Josiah provided small livestock for the Passover offering for the entire assembly.
The priests slaughtered the Passover lamb for all who had returned from exile.
The prophecy concerning the Lord's suffering servant, who is led like a lamb to the slaughter.
John the Baptist points to Jesus as the Lamb of God who takes away the sin of the world.
Christ is our Passover lamb, sacrificed, fulfilling the type of the Passover lamb in Egypt.
Believers are redeemed with Christ's precious blood, like that of a lamb without defect or blemish.
John sees a lamb standing as though it had been slaughtered, right in the center before the throne.
Exodus 12 establishes the specific Passover lamb as a historical precursor to the general sacrificial rules in Leviticus 1.
Contrast between the original permission for each family's Passover lamb and later restrictions to centralize slaughter.
Parallel in the requirement for unblemished animals (lamb, goat, or ox) for holy consecration and salvation rituals.
